findings: Q1: the original reloads the accounts pointer before 10/19 AccountInfo clones (main 3/19). No matched window comes close: holder_distribution (loop) 5/13, every other multi-clone CPI build holds the pointer. RA pressure only, no idiom.

Q2: all 46 matched 7/8/8/8/1 piece copies are Ok payloads of Result<Pubkey,E> (core result.rs:1952 Try::branch or Ok(..)); the Err payload at 8..24 splits SROA on the 8-byte grid. The admin_cto entry load of new on that grid (orig 0x4d8-0x538) appears nowhere else.
Shape uniqueness: 43% of the 4-grams covering admin_cto's orig-only runs occur in no matched window (19% for the whole original function).

Some(new) without the args tuple collapses (0.48104) only because new's tag is then loaded inside the sharing arm; main's args tuple loads it early, at the original's position (orig 0x4d8). Same 281 blocks and alloca set; rfj LCS 2985 -> 2414.

sharing_update=Some(args.0.map(|_|target)) reproduces the original sharing-CPI val copy shape (tag + 7/8/8/8/1 from the validated target), rfj only -45 vs main and the original's frame bottom -0xc38, but spill slots move (360 frame accesses off vs 121): 0.54993 @27,352. match/if spellings are byte-identical.
Dropping main's Ok::<_,Error>((target,sharing_update,cashback))? round trip costs 0.12 (m_nt 0.55019): it is a frame-order construct; it does nothing for valmap (vm_nt 0.55022).

Q4: the sibling create_v2::execute writes the same fee checks followed by fee=creator_fee_bps.0 in the OK path, i.e. a validated-fee local; this confirms w15a29's fee-tag phi reading of the original OK block (priced below main by w15a29/w15a15).

Both Q2 classes are reproducible by ordinary spellings (entry pieces: validate reads args.0, w13a41; val copy: Some(args.0.map(|_|target))), but neither survives on today's skeleton (mA 0.43917 @27584, vmA 0.4494 @27824); the original gets both from its per-arm threaded validate.
